en.headline: Kau Kee opens first retail shop after 66 years supplying fish balls to eateries
en.dek: The Mong Kok factory that has long supplied nearly 1,000 local stalls and restaurants now sells its signature fish balls and snacks directly to the public.
body: Kau Kee Food Factory, a Mong Kok producer that has supplied fish balls to almost 1,000 eateries and snack stalls across Hong Kong for 66 years, opened its first retail shop late last year so members of the public can buy the products that were previously available only through the trade.

Second-generation owner Anita Lee Yan-kwan, a former civil servant who took over the family business during the pandemic, said most people on the street would not recognise the Kau Kee name even though almost every Hongkonger had probably eaten its fish balls at some point. The shop sells the factory’s signature springy fish balls along with other snacks such as fish siu mai and cuttlefish balls at prices below typical restaurant mark-ups.

Lee said the retail move was intended both to let customers buy the products without the usual intermediary markup and to raise the profile of a long-running local maker. The shop is at 49A Bute Street in Mong Kok.

zh.headline: 九記魚蛋廠66年後開首間零售店 直接售予市民
zh.dek: 長年供應近千間食肆及小食檔的旺角魚蛋廠，去年底開設首間零售店，市民可直接購買招牌魚蛋及小食。
body: 經營66年的九記食品廠長期為全港近千間食肆及小食檔供應魚蛋，去年底在旺角開設首間零售店，讓市民直接購買以往只供業內的產品。
第二代負責人李欣君（Anita Lee）曾任公務員，疫情期間接手家族生意。她表示，街坊未必聽過「九記」這個名字，但幾乎每個香港人都可能吃過其魚蛋。店內出售招牌彈牙魚蛋，以及魚肉燒賣、墨魚丸等小食，售價較一般食肆加價後為低。
李欣君指開設零售店既方便市民以較低價錢購買，亦希望提高這家長年本地廠商的知名度。店址位於旺角碧街49A號。
